  def self.wrap(&computation)
    raise ArgumentError, "a block is required" unless computation
    memoized = nil
    computed = false
    proc do |*args, &block|
      if !computed
        memoized = computation.call(*args, &block)
        computed = true
      end
      memoized
    end
  end
end

```ruby
class Distance
  include Comparable

  attr_reader :meters

  def initialize(meters)
    @meters = meters
  end

  def -(other)
    if other.is_a?(Distance)
      Distance.new(@meters - other.meters)
    elsif other.is_a?(Integer)
      Distance.new(@meters - other)
    else
      raise ArgumentError, "Unsupported type for subtraction: #{other.class}"
    end
  end

  def +(other)
    if other.is_a?(Distance)
      Distance.new(@meters + other.meters)
    elsif other.is_a?(Integer)
      Distance.new(@meters + other)
    else
      raise ArgumentError, "Unsupported type for addition: #{other.class}"
    end
  end

  def ==(other)
    return false unless other.is_a?(Distance)
    @meters == other.meters
  end

  def <=>(other)
    return nil unless other.is_a?(Distance)
    @meters <=> other.meters
  end

  def to_i
    @meters
  end

  def to_s
    "#{@meters}m"
  end
end

# Extend Integer to support subtraction of Distance
class Integer
  def -(other)
    if other.is_a?(Distance)
      Distance.new(self - other.meters)
    else
      super
    end
  end

  def +(other)
    if other.is_a?(Distance)
      Distance.new(self + other.meters)
    else
      super
    end
  end
end
```

class SparseArray
  include Enumerable

  def initialize
    @values = {}
  end

  def [](index, value = :unset)
    if value == :unset
      @values[index]
    else
      @values[index] = value
    end
  end

  def each
    return enum_for unless block_given?
    
    @values.keys.sort.each do |index|
      yield @values[index]
    end
  end
end

Calling #each with a block yields from, from - 1, from - 2, and so on down to 1, in that order, to the block, and #each returns the Steps instance itself. Calling #each with no block returns an object that can be driven one value at a time by repeatedly calling #next on it - returning from, then from - 1, and so on down to 1, then raising StopIteration on any further call. That same no-block return value also supports #with_index (pairing each value with its zero-based position) and #to_a (collecting every value into an array), both reflecting the identical from, from - 1, ..., 1 sequence.

message.content:
I'll implement the `Steps` class step by step, then verify with a test.

```ruby
class Steps
  def initialize(from)
    raise ArgumentError, "from must be a positive integer" unless from.is_a?(Integer) && from > 0
    @from = from
    @current = from
  end

  # With a block: yield from, from-1, ..., 1 and return self
  def each(&block)
    if block
      i = @from
      while i >= 1
        block.call(i)
        i -= 1
      end
      self
    else
      # Return an object driven by #next, supporting #with_index and #to_a
      iterator = Iterator.new(@from)
      iterator
    end
  end

  # Internal iterator driven by #next
  class Iterator
    def initialize(from)
      @from = from
      @current = from
    end

    def next
      if @current < 1
        raise StopIteration
      end
      value = @current
      @current -= 1
      value
    end

    # Pair each value with its zero-based position
    def with_index
      iter = Iterator.new(@from)
      idx = 0
      Enumerator.new do |yielder|
        loop do
          v = iter.next
          yielder << [v, idx]
          idx += 1
        end
      rescue StopIteration
        break
      end
    end

    # Collect every value into an array
    def to_a
      arr = []
      iter = Iterator.new(@from)
      loop do
        arr << iter.next
      rescue StopIteration
        break
      end
      arr
    end
  end
end
```
